decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom extends the firm's core dosimetry and scanning-system expertise into a growing proton therapy segment, and with its release only just scheduled for Q1/2019 it is far too early to judge results.
Small volume ionization chambers sit at the centre of the firm's decades of dosimetry knowledge and accredited calibration capability, so it can readily interpret feedback and refine the product.
A second small volume chamber fills a related niche in small-field dosimetry that the firm understands well, and a portfolio of chamber variants is typical of established dosimetry suppliers.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a staple product that builds directly on the firm's core competence and calibration services, so dropping it would make little sense.
A relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantoms and QA software, which strengthens the integrated workflow the firm is pursuing.

Thimble chambers are long-established dosimetry instruments closely tied to the firm's existing knowledge base and service infrastructure, giving it strong capacity to sustain and improve the product.
